<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d9be915f4080038132858708150dcd1ee84bc0bd`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d9be915f4080038132858708150dcd1ee84bc0bd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `02a52e78c66c8a8992f62792d6661e1c7053e7d8` — the merge of head `b9ce479e6de7a98539ebcd5cebdb787bc40a471c` into base `d9be915f4080038132858708150dcd1ee84bc0bd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 02a52e78c66c8a8992f62792d6661e1c7053e7d8 && git checkout 02a52e78c66c8a8992f62792d6661e1c7053e7d8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d9be915f4080038132858708150dcd1ee84bc0bd b9ce479e6de7a98539ebcd5cebdb787bc40a471c && git checkout -B drift-repro d9be915f4080038132858708150dcd1ee84bc0bd && git merge --no-ff b9ce479e6de7a98539ebcd5cebdb787bc40a471c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d9be915f4080038132858708150dcd1ee84bc0bd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d9be915f4080038132858708150dcd1ee84bc0bd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibyQBB3KuDoNobNq9LH

## Seat check

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-C) at head `e5a7e08b934241bb2a835b29c85c1d6bc5e5cc8d`, read 2026-11-20T07:50Z.

- **One record is owed before landing, with no new head:** the claim amendment (below).
- **One L2 is owed:** CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER, covering the `packages/spec/src/**` describe text and the published `@objectstack/formula` answer change. d7-C runs it as an isolated reviewer in parallel. This ACCEPT does not replace it.

### Owed before landing (a record, not code)

**Amend the claim's file surface.** Claim 7030625057 names `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx`, its tests and one changeset ("stop on breach; explain in the report"). The head also edits:

- `celAuthoring.ts`;
- `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`, plus three regenerated reference pages;
- `packages/formula/src/formula-return.ts` and its test.

The dev reports explain each widening (7032209353, 7033149333), and each is needed by the fix:

- the lazy seam keeps cel-js out of the main bundle;
- the spec prose would otherwise be false;
- the formula change is your ruling A.

But the claim is what other seats' pre-claim and overlap checks read, and `field.zod.ts` and `formula-return.ts` are shared surfaces. Post an amendment naming them before landing, as d7-A did for #35758 (7031864853), and re-run `overlap-check` after it. This needs no delta L1.

### Your ruling A: `inferFormulaReturn` answers `{}`, never `number`, for an unprovable money operand

Agreed. The inspector can only withdraw a declared `currency` safely on an answer that means "proved not money". Before this change, `number` also covered "read an amount but could not follow it". Splitting the two is what makes the withdraw sound.

- **Code.**
  - `readsMoneyOperand` runs only when the numeric path's `dimOf` answers `unproven`. A proven plain number, such as a same-currency ratio (`QUANTITY`) or a ternary of constants, still answers `number`.
  - `isMoneyTyped` counts a `currency` field, a formula declared `currency`, and a `summary` whose `function` is not `count`. The roll-up's source type is not on this object, so `min` / `max` / `sum` / `avg` are conservatively possible money. `function` is the `summaryOperations` key (`field.zod.ts`).
- **Callers.** The only in-repo caller of the changed answer is the new inspector seam (`git grep inferFormulaReturn` outside tests and docs). The changeset gives external callers the FROM/TO and the migration line (read `inferExpressionType` instead).
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` hold. No accept set widens and no export is added. The output change is on a function no metadata author writes, and the `returnType` value's meaning is unchanged. The L2 judges the published-answer face.

### Code (inspector)

- **Async ordering.** The money verdict arrives after the render that settled the CEL verdicts. Three checks keep a stale verdict from writing:
  - `formulaVerdictRef.current !== now` drops a superseded one;
  - `stampFormulaTypeRef` runs the latest render's closure, so `def` is current;
  - `stampFormulaType` re-checks the field name and that the source still equals the draft's expression.
- **Decision order.**
  - A declared `percent` returns first under `number` / unproven.
  - A proven-money verdict stamps `currency` with its config.
  - A declared `currency` under `number` / unproven is withdrawn only when the money verdict itself answers `number`. Unproven, or no engine verdict (`null`), keeps it.
  - Everything else stamps the proven CEL type.
  - `currencyConfig` travels with `currency` only: deleted otherwise, written as the proven one otherwise. `sameFlatRecord` avoids a no-op write.
  - The write is a whole `writeDef(nextDef)` built from the latest `def`.
- **Failure handling.** `inferFormulaReturnDeclaration` answers `null` ("no verdict", never "not money") for empty input, a missing export or a throw. It copies `currencyConfig`, so the stamp never aliases the engine's object.

### Tests and controls

- **Inspector pins** (real `inferFormulaReturn` behind the stub):
  - the card's repro drops `currency` and its config;
  - a still-money edit keeps `currency` with the proven USD config;
  - a `number` formula edited into money is stamped `currency` with USD;
  - unproven cases keep `currency` (the field-over-field quotient, the `sum` roll-up);
  - a new formula over an unprovable amount stamps the CEL type `number`;
  - CONTROLS: a declared `percent` is kept; a proven `boolean` stamps over `currency` and drops the config.
- **Formula pins:**
  - each changeset FROM shape answers `{}`;
  - CONTROLS: proven money still stamps with config, quantities still `number`, a `count` roll-up still `number`.
- **Ablations**, each restored blob-equal:
  - A, the withdraw branch: the repro is red.
  - B, the money-proof branch: the `number`→money pin is red.
  - C, the producer's unproven branch: "each answers `{}`" is red.
  - The A attempt the tool refused (13 matches) was recorded as a no-op, not counted.
- **On the keep pins.** They assert after `settle()` (600 ms) rather than on a signal that the money verdict landed. The keep guard (`declared?.returnType !== 'number'`) has no inspector-level ablation; ablation C covers its producer side. This is acceptable because the keep behaviour predates this PR ("as before") and the guard is one line. I note it because a later timing change could make those pins pass vacuously.

### Prose, sentence by sentence

- **Changeset (app-shell).** Each sentence matches the code and a pin:
  - provable money stamps `currency` with the source currency (absent for the tenant default), from `number` too;
  - a `number` answer withdraws and drops the config;
  - unproven, or an engine without the export, keeps;
  - `percent` is unchanged;
  - text / boolean / date stamp and now drop a stale config;
  - the stamp runs only after an expression edit.
- **Changeset (formula).** Every FROM example traces through `dimOf`:
  - the `sum` roll-up times a constant;
  - `100 / amount`;
  - `amount % 3`;
  - two currencies summed;
  - `double(a) * double(b)` (a money×money product);
  - an unparseable `currencyConfig` (`fieldDim` → unproven).

  Each now reads a money operand on an unproven path, so it answers `{}`. "A ratio of two amounts in one currency is unchanged" and "a `count` roll-up … as before" also hold.
- **`field.zod.ts`.** The JSDoc and the `.describe()` both say the same thing: `currency` is stamped when proven, withdrawn for `number` with its config dropped, and kept under unproven. That matches the inspector. The three regenerated reference pages carry the new `.describe()` verbatim, and `check:generated` is green in CI.

### Nits (not owed)

1. `readsMoneyOperand` also scans a ternary's condition, which never reaches the value. So `record.amount > 100 ? size(record.lines) : 0` now answers `{}` instead of `number`. This is the conservative direction, but skipping `args[0]` of `?:` would keep `number` for a count gated on an amount.
2. `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx` says "You declare it yourself — nothing back-fills it" about `returnType`. Studio's stamp already wrote `number` / `text` / … on an edit before this PR, and now writes `currency` as well. This is pre-existing and outside this card, but the sentence could say "nothing back-fills it at runtime; Studio stamps it as you edit".

### Gates and routing

- CI at `e5a7e08b`: 74 check runs, 63 `success` and 11 `skipped`, none red.
- After the claim amendment and the CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 PASS on this head, `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35774` decides the landing route.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Round-1 open question (a roll-up read answers `number`: accept, or fix the producer).** Ruled A by the lane PM, as the PR body records, and implemented (`formula-return.ts:276-279` and `:356`), pinned at the producer and at the inspector. Answered as asked. The ruling's principle is not met on other operand routes: M1.
- **File surface beyond the claim** (`celAuthoring.ts`; the spec text and three regenerated pages; the `packages/formula` producer and its test; `spec` and `formula` in the changeset). Accepted. The seam file is where every engine verdict is feature-detected and stubbed. The spec text stated the rule this change reverses. The producer change is ruling A. The spec touch is why this record is owed.

**What was tried, and what held.**

| Probe | Result |

| Unproven verdict | Holds: the declared `currency` and its config stay. Pinned (field-over-field quotient). |
| `percent` never withdrawn | Holds by reading: the guard returns before the money verdict is read. The PR's own CONTROL cannot fail (S1) and the published text does not say it (S2). The two #35047 pins, with no money verdict, are live. |

| A formula over a currency formula | Holds: proven with the operand's config (`record.weighted * 2`, pinned). Unproven over one answers `{}` by reading; no shape discriminates that leg (M1's fix list). |

**Does the spec text say exactly what the inspector does?** Yes, except for `percent` under a money verdict (S2). Its sentence "answering `number`: the expression no longer computes money" becomes true when M1 is fixed.

**Does the producer header say exactly what the code does?** No: M1 and S3.

**Are the pins one per shape with a CONTROL?** At the producer, sixteen sources are each asserted under their own message in one case, with CONTROLs for proven money, quantities and a `count` roll-up; ablation C is red. The gaps are in M1's fix list. At the inspector, eight cases, one of them vacuous: S1.

M1 (must-fix) — a `number` answer is not yet "proved not money", and the inspector withdraws on it. `readsMoneyOperand` and `isMoneyTyped` (`formula-return.ts:271-296`) see a money operand only as `record.NAME` or a bare `NAME` whose host field is `currency`, a formula with `returnType: 'currency'`, or a non-`count` `summary`. Any other read leaves the unit proof unproven, finds no money operand and falls to the plain inference, which types `dyn * double` as `number` (`packages/formula/src/validate.test.ts:1255` on `main`). Four routes:

- (a) **One hop through a reference field**: `record.account.balance * 0.9`, `record.opportunity.amount * 0.1`. A formula `expression` is a site where one hop is served (`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`, #24197: the read path preloads it). `dimOf` is unproven because the base is not `record`; `readsMoneyOperand` then asks `isMoneyTyped('account')`, a lookup: false. The leaf's type is not on this object, which is the header's own reason for reading a `summary` as possibly money.
- (b) **A formula operand that declares no `returnType`**: `record.subtotal * 0.2` over `subtotal: { type: 'formula' }`. `fieldDim` is unproven; `isMoneyTyped` tests `returnType === 'currency'`: false. This is the installed base. On `main` Studio clears `returnType` on every field-over-field formula (`record.amount + record.tax` types `dyn`), and hand-written formulas often carry none (`days_to_close` in `examples/app-crm`).
- (c) **The other spellings of one read**: `record['amount'] * 0.1`, and the optional forms `.?` and `[?]`. `asMember` in `relationship-traversal.ts` treats the four as the same read; `readsMoneyOperand` matches `.` alone, so the object's own `currency` field goes unseen.
- (d) **A name the map does not declare**: `record.unknown_field * 2` is still pinned `number`, under a title that says the expression "reads no amount" (`formula-return.test.ts:116-125`). CI ran that pin green on this head; (b) takes the same two branches.

In Studio, (a), (b) and (c) lint clean (`checkFieldExistence` judges the head segment, and `lintCelPredicate` passes no field types) and type `number`. So `stampFormulaType` (`ObjectFieldInspector.tsx:1151-1156`) reads `declared.returnType === 'number'`, writes `number` and deletes `currencyConfig`. A `currency` the author declared by hand on such a formula, which is the only way it can be declared since no proof reaches it, is gone after the next expression edit (`0.1` to `0.12`). On `main` it survived. Route (d) cannot reach the stamp: the editor refuses an unknown field.

This is the round-1 question on more routes, and ruling A already answers it: the producer makes `number` mean proven. Until it does, three sentences are false: the header (`formula-return.ts:51-56`), the function doc (`:318-321`) and the changeset's "always means".
